sourceNote: A copy of assets/models/badger/badger-edit.glb (armSource) with new quad tubes on each arm from the shoulder line to the wrist. tools/blender/arm_rebuild.py makes these faces, and finds the shoulder line at 0.1 of the upper arm. The other faces stay as in the copy.
armSourceNote: The copy of assets/models/badger/badger.glb with the arms free of the trunk (tools/blender/badger_edit.py, assets/models/badger/README.md). Git keeps it out, and tools/blender/arm_rebuild.py reads it.
paintedNote: The weights of the clavicles and the arms are the automatic weights of Blender with the weight rules of tools/blender/arm_rebuild.py. The vertices on the bones of paintedLower keep the rule weights, as on the monkey.

armSegments.note: Each upper arm and each forearm has 4 deform segments, and each elbow and wrist a helper bone. The helper is twice the gap of the elbow rings of tools/blender/arm_rebuild.py (step_skeleton() prints it).
armSegments.rootSegmentNote: The rule weight of each upper arm goes to its first segment (segment_joints() and main() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), so that the trunk around the socket takes the roll of the first ring of the tube.

name: Badger

app.note: The size of the parametric badger: the head top is at 1.038 m. The skull top of the mesh is its highest point at the middle plane (1.0 u). The reach goes from the shoulder joint to the middle of the palm.

armFactorNote: The arms keep the length of the mesh. With the factor 1, the reach from the shoulder joint to the middle of the palm is 0.273 m. This reach gets to each strike of the bass drum, the snare drum, and the small percussion.
legFactorNote: The legs keep the length of the mesh, with no stretch.
jointsNote: The places are in the units and the axes of the studio in the source pose: 1 unit from the soles to the skull top, +z forward, +x the left side. The right side mirrors the left side. Each roll is the hint of the z axis of the bone. The joints from the elbow to the finger tips are the joints of the arm that tools/blender/badger_edit.py turns 8 degrees out (it prints them). SOURCE_ARM of the script keeps the joints of the source.

studio.bindArmsNote: With straightArms, bindArms.upper_arm sets the bind upper arm, along the upper arm of the turned copy, and bindArms.forearm sets only the elbow axis: the cross product of the bind upper arm and this forearm direction (StudioBody.hinges, bind_hinges() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The axis stays within 2 degrees of the axis of the old bent bind, so that the zero of the roll of the upper arm stays. A bind upper arm 39 degrees above the source arm crumpled the hanging arm roots.
studio.straightArmsNote: The bind keeps the arms of the source straight: the forearm and the paw keep the turn of the upper arm, so that the rest shape holds the bend of no role (the role-neutral bind of design 4.4).
studio.bindSupinationNote: The bind paw of each arm turns about its bind forearm toward supination, the left 60 degrees and the right 45 degrees (paw_supination() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The rule of design 4.4 (pnpm bind-supination badger) gives about 120 and 90 degrees. The own roles win: with the left 123 degrees, the forearm twist p95 of the xylophonist L is 86 (limit 80), and with 90 and 90 degrees, the wrist rings of the snare drummer and the cymbalist narrow by up to 1.7 mm. A second probe of the rig at 60 and 45 degrees gives the same rule values.
studio.note: legTurns gives the world turn of each left leg bone from the seated bind to the source: the thigh slopes 25 degrees down and turns 15 degrees out, and the shin is vertical (tools/rig/leg_turns.py <config> 25 15 0). The app takes the standing body.

sliver.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, and the wolf.

line.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, and the wolf.

haunch.note: The part of the thigh weight that goes to the hips grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height, so that the buttocks stay on the hips.

weights.rigidNote: The corners of each thin face at these points take the mean of their weights (rigid_faces() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The points are the middles of slivers at the front of the left shoulder, in the left armpit, and on the right paw (pnpm fold-probe <role> --faces).
weights.note: Beyond the plane |x| = armSplit, only the free arm follows the arm bones. Above headFrom (the chin), each vertex follows the head only. The round ears follow the head (earBase). The tail ball holds the short tail behind the plane z = behind (tailBall).
weights.rigidPaintedNote: The faces at these points take the mean of the painted weights of their corners, as rigid does for the rule weights. The first item holds two faces with a corner of less than 1 degree at the right shoulder line, and the last item a thin face between the right paw and the claws. The other items are thin faces at the shoulder lines. Each of these faces folded in each sample of the bass drummer, the percussionist, or the xylophonist (pnpm fold-probe <role> --faces).

raise.note: The shape of the raised arm L of the percussionist (pnpm raise-fit). It corrects 10 faces at the front of the left shoulder, which fold in each sample of the triangle when the upper arm turns 98 degrees from the bind.

The shape of the raised arm L of the flutist@badger (pnpm raise-fit). The shared hold turns the upper arm 119 degrees from the bind, and the front and the top of the arm root fold (faces 586 to 1059 of the note of raiseNote) in each sample of the play.

The shape of the raised arm L of the clarinetist@badger (pnpm raise-fit). The shared hold turns the upper arm 118 degrees from the bind, and the front and the top of the arm root fold (faces 586 to 1059 of the note of raiseNote) in each sample of the play. It also holds the trumpeter@badger.

The shape of the raised arm R of the flutist@badger (pnpm raise-fit). The shared hold turns the upper arm 112 degrees from the bind, and the front of the right arm root folds (faces 539, 540, 692, 693, 697 to 699, 743, 744, 1109, and 2391) in each sample of the play. It also holds the trumpeter@badger.

raiseNote: Corrective shapes of a raised arm (pnpm raise-fit). The first is the left arm that holds the triangle up: the straight bind turns the upper arm about 98 degrees from the bind there. The next two are the left arm of the shared flute and clarinet holds of a recast badger, at about 118 degrees, and the last is the right arm of the flute hold. There the clavicle turns about 23 degrees, and the faces at the front and the top of the arm root (586, 587, 591, 630, 631, 636, 650, 651, 909, 976 to 978, 1020, 1021, 1424, 1577, 1058, and 1059) fold. A shape of the cellist@badger (101 degrees) also turned over 4 more faces in the play of the percussionist, so the cello has no shape. The four shapes are the limit of a body.

flip.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, and the wolf.

refine.ringsNote: The config has no rings. pnpm rig-mesh badger --check lists the thin faces near the joints as candidates for a ring (check.thin).

check.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, and the wolf.

colors.note: A face is dark when at least eyeShare of its samples have a linear luminance below dark. The dark front fur and the black eye stripes are near 0.02, so dark is 0.01: only the pupils and the smile line are dark. Each face keeps the colors of the texture.

eyeShell.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, and the wolf.

chair.note: The seat is level, and its top is the lowest point of the seated body over the seat, with no shin, foot, or tail. The half width holds the haunch (x 0.22). The app takes the standing body, so the chair only sets the seated bind.

crease.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, and the wolf.

sit.note: The values of the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, and the wolf.
